name: Pat Harris
q1: I’m up early without an alarm, grab coffee, and go wander somewhere with fresh air. No agenda, just movement and sun. If I end the day a little sweaty and a little calm, that’s a good Sunday.
q2: I want to talk it out honestly, but I try to do it with care. I’ll say how I feel without making it a character attack. I don’t bottle stuff, but I also don’t scream.
q3: Refilling my water bottle with ice until it’s “perfect.” It feels like resetting my whole system.
q4: I look outgoing, but I actually get nervous meeting new people and overthink what I said after.
q5: When someone notices effort. “Text me when you get home,” “Did you eat?” — that tiny check-in melts me.

name: Aria Ramirez
q1: Pajamas, pancakes, and music playing in the kitchen while I half-clean and half-dance. I like feeding people and having the house smell warm.
q2: I cool off first. If we talk while I’m still hot, I’ll cry or shut down. Give me ten minutes, then I’m all about “Okay, how do we fix this?”
q3: Wiping down the counters until they’re shiny. It’s therapeutic in a way that’s almost embarrassing.
q4: I’ll act calm and capable all day, but I’m actually very soft and get sentimental fast.
q5: When someone asks, “Who’s taking care of you?” and actually means it.

name: Mei Harris
q1: Headphones, something creative in my hands, and zero plans. I love letting myself drift — sketching, messing with sound loops, writing lines that might never turn into anything.
q2: I need a minute alone to sort out what I actually feel versus what I blurted in the moment. After that, I’ll tell you the truth, even if it’s awkward.
q3: The click of a good pen on smooth paper. I could literally do that for hours.
q4: People assume I’m chill, but I actually feel everything very loudly. I just don’t always show it right away.
q5: When someone asks follow-up questions about the weird thing I’m making, instead of just saying “that’s cool” and moving on.

name: Sage Cooper
q1: I like running my little systems — laundry going, meals prepped for the week, bills handled — and then I reward myself by doing absolutely nothing for the rest of the day.
q2: I don’t like guessing games. Tell me what’s off, I’ll listen, and I’ll tell you what I can change. I’m not great with passive-aggressive hints.
q3: Organizing the fridge so everything lines up. It feels like my brain finally stops buzzing.
q4: I look practical, but I’m secretly romantic. I remember dates, small comments, all of it.
q5: When someone notices the invisible work — planning, cleaning, keeping things steady — and doesn’t act like it’s automatic.

name: Zara Rodriguez
q1: Perfect Sunday is friends on the couch, some ridiculous snack combo we swore we wouldn’t eat, and us roasting each other in the nicest possible way. Bonus points if there’s a nap in there.
q2: My first instinct is to joke to keep it from getting too heavy. But if it’s real, I’ll drop the jokes and just ask, “Okay, are we good or not?” I hate letting bad energy sit.
q3: When a song lines up with how I’m walking and suddenly I feel like I have theme music.
q4: I come off loud, but I’m actually really loyal and pay attention to what people need.
q5: When someone can match my energy — laugh with me, but also sit with me when I go quiet.

name: Ricardo Bennett
q1: Give me a book, a hoodie, and a corner where I can exist without small talk. That, and maybe a slow walk later with headphones in, just letting my brain wander.
q2: I don’t like yelling. I’d rather step back, figure out what the actual problem is, and talk like we both want to fix it instead of win it.
q3: Finding the perfect sentence in a random article and saving it like a treasure.
q4: I look calm and analytical, but I’m actually sentimental in this quiet way. I keep screenshots of nice messages.
q5: When someone doesn’t take it personally that I need space sometimes, and lets me come back on my own.

name: Kiaan Brooks
q1: Honestly? Errands. I’ll hit the store, get the car washed, knock out the boring stuff, and then finally let myself sit and breathe. That’s my way of feeling in control before Monday.
q2: I’ll hear you out. I don’t interrupt, I don’t get dramatic. But I expect the same respect back, because I’m not here to be talked over.
q3: Crossing something off a to-do list. I’ll even write things I already did just to cross them off.
q4: People assume I’m serious all the time, but I’m actually kind of goofy once I trust you.
q5: When someone notices the way I keep things running and says “Thank you,” not “Finally.”

name: Jada Jordan
q1: Wake up early, go somewhere with sky and air, move my body until my brain stops spinning, then eat something huge and unearned. That’s peace for me.
q2: I’ll be honest, even if it’s uncomfortable. I can take “this hurt me” way better than cold distance or guessing.
q3: Maps. I love looking at maps and imagining routes I haven’t taken yet.
q4: I save little voice memos to myself when I feel proud or scared, so I remember what it felt like.
q5: When someone gets excited with me instead of trying to calm me down.

name: Akira Le
q1: Cooking something slow, music in the background, my phone face down. I like creating that little bubble where everyone feels welcome to just exist.
q2: I try to understand where you’re coming from first. I’ll fight for us, but I won’t fight against you.
q3: When leftovers stack up in perfect little containers. It’s silly but it makes me feel stable.
q4: People come to me for comfort, but I actually carry a lot that I don’t say out loud.
q5: When someone notices I’m tired without me having to be “the strong one” all the time.

name: Laura Lee
q1: Headphones on, zoning out in my own little world, maybe wandering through the neighborhood just people-watching. I like being around life without having to perform.
q2: I’ll tell you the truth, but I need you to talk to me like I’m your teammate, not your opponent. I shut down if it turns into “win/lose.”
q3: When streetlights hit puddles at night and everything looks kind of cinematic for a second.
q4: I act low-key, but I feel things sharply. I just edit before I speak.
q5: When someone listens past the first layer and doesn’t make me explain why I feel the way I feel.

name: Zara Robinson
q1: Sundays are my guilt-free recharge day. I’ll make a messy breakfast, scroll too long, and then wander outside just to feel the air. It’s the only day where “doing nothing” feels like progress.
q2: I hate raised voices. If we’re off, I’d rather take a short walk, breathe, and come back ready to actually listen.
q3: Fresh sheets that are still a little warm from the dryer.
q4: I keep playlists for every emotion — even irritation has its own soundtrack.
q5: When someone remembers the tiny things I mention and brings them up weeks later.

name: Carlos Ramirez
q1: I cook something that takes hours just because I can. The house smells amazing, and I get to share leftovers with whoever drops by.
q2: I’ll ask questions until I understand the “why.” Once that clicks, I’m calm.
q3: The sound of my dog snoring next to me.
q4: I pretend I’m extroverted, but I’m secretly happiest in quiet company.
q5: When someone notices my effort before I talk about it.

name: Gloria Patel
q1: Coffee, a walk around the block, and then back under a blanket to read half a book and nap through the rest.
q2: I write notes in my phone first — it keeps me from saying things I’ll regret.
q3: Organizing my spice rack by color instead of alphabet.
q4: I tear up at good commercials; I’m that person.
q5: When someone laughs at my dry jokes instead of asking if I’m being serious.

name: Takeshi Kim
q1: Morning yoga, strong espresso, and pretending I don’t have emails waiting. If I touch my laptop, the day’s ruined.
q2: I stay calm until I feel dismissed — then I shut down. I’m learning to speak up before that point.
q3: Perfectly foamed milk. I’ll restart the machine until I nail it.
q4: I keep handwritten letters from friends in a shoebox; it’s my secret therapy.
q5: When someone tells me they feel safe around me. That’s everything.

name: Curtis Brown
q1: Up late, brunch late, everything late. The world can wait while I wander through the day in slippers.
q2: I’m direct — not rude, just honest. Life’s too short for guessing games.
q3: When my toast pops up at the exact same time my song ends.
q4: I’m a huge nerd for crossword puzzles; they calm me down.
q5: When someone laughs at the weird little tangents I go on instead of tuning them out.

name: Sofia Park
q1: I like mixing rest with progress — laundry folded, plants watered, then a movie marathon with no shame.
q2: I need to cool off alone first; otherwise I say things sharper than I mean.
q3: The smell of rain on pavement — it resets me instantly.
q4: I look confident, but compliments actually make me awkward.
q5: When someone notices I’m overthinking and says, “It’s okay, you did enough.”

name: Isabela Watson
q1: Coffee, sunlight, and a podcast I only half listen to. My favorite part is the quiet between things.
q2: I ask for a pause instead of storming off — silence helps me find words that don’t sting.
q3: Rewatching old sitcoms and quoting lines under my breath.
q4: I talk in my sleep — full conversations apparently.
q5: When someone gets that “space” doesn’t mean “distance.”

name: Anjali Howard
q1: I’ll drive with no destination, windows down, playlist loud. It’s like therapy but cheaper.
q2: I go logical first — what’s the root, what’s the fix — then circle back to feelings.
q3: Perfect parallel parking on the first try.
q4: I love bad reality TV. It helps me turn my brain off.
q5: When someone challenges me without trying to win.

name: Hana Davis
q1: Cooking breakfast for someone else. There’s something grounding about feeding people I care about.
q2: I’ll listen before I talk, but I’ll expect the same. Fair is fair.
q3: Washing dishes with music blasting — I turn it into karaoke.
q4: I’m a hopeless romantic but pretend I’m too busy for it.
q5: When someone meets my sarcasm with warmth, not confusion.

name: Grayson Sharma
q1: Sleep in, stretch, no alarms, no plans. The goal is to feel unproductive and proud of it.
q2: I’d rather talk things through than stew. I can’t sleep with tension hanging in the air.
q3: Peeling stickers off new electronics perfectly clean.
q4: I still write in a paper planner; crossing things off feels good.
q5: When someone lets me ramble through an idea before fixing it.

name: Jordan Alvarez
q1: I start with coffee and a slow scroll through playlists until one sticks. Then I cook breakfast way too big for one person and save the rest for Monday lunch.
q2: I need eye contact and calm voices. I shut down fast if it turns into a debate club.
q3: Untangling necklaces — I get weirdly proud when I fix the impossible knot.
q4: I seem easy-going, but I’m quietly competitive about everything.
q5: When someone gets excited about the same small victories I do.

name: Neha Miller
q1: Morning walk, farmers-market fruit, and calling my mom while chopping something. It’s the one day I actually slow down enough to taste food.
q2: I ask for clarity, not volume. If we can explain the why, the rest usually softens.
q3: The smell of oranges on my hands after peeling them.
q4: I remember random details about people — birthdays, coffee orders, dog names.
q5: When someone notices I’m caring even when I act casual.

name: Hudson Iqbal
q1: Coffee, cat in lap, window cracked for fresh air. I read until the cat decides it’s snack time.
q2: I write my thoughts first; seeing them on screen helps me be kinder out loud.
q3: Perfectly aligned margins in a document — yes, I’m that person.
q4: I come across quiet, but my group chat knows I’m the chaos agent.
q5: When someone gets my humor without needing translation.

name: Charles Walker
q1: I’ll bake something I don’t need just because the smell makes the place feel alive. Then I share it with neighbors I barely know.
q2: I like direct talk followed by a hug or at least a smile. Closure matters more than being right.
q3: Watching dough rise. Feels like magic every time.
q4: I grew up shy — still surprised people call me social now.
q5: When someone thanks me for things I didn’t announce I was doing.

name: Vikram Patel
q1: Headphones, longboard, aimless ride until I find sunlight worth stopping in.
q2: I can handle disagreement, just not disrespect. Keep it calm, keep it honest.
q3: Fresh notebook smell. First page pressure is real.
q4: I act chill, but I plan everything two steps ahead.
q5: When someone matches my pace instead of trying to slow me down.

name: Liliana Bryant
q1: I deep-clean something random, then reward myself with pancakes and cartoons. Balance.
q2: I need to laugh eventually — tension dissolves when humor sneaks back in.
q3: Finding old receipts from good nights out.
q4: I sing badly but loudly in the car, zero shame.
q5: When someone laughs at my corny jokes like they actually find me funny.

name: Amir Kermani
q1: I scroll Zillow for houses I’ll never buy, then go water my single plant. Dreams and realism in one morning.
q2: I take a breather and then circle back — I’d rather repair than score points.
q3: Matching socks fresh out of the dryer.
q4: I love spreadsheets; order makes me calm.
q5: When someone appreciates reliability as much as spontaneity.

name: Adriana Zhang
q1: I wander the flea market, not buying much, just touching textures and people-watching.
q2: I listen longer than I talk. Usually the solution shows up in the silence.
q3: Finding a weird mug and imagining who owned it before.
q4: I’m sentimental about objects; I can’t throw out ticket stubs.
q5: When someone asks about the stories behind my clutter instead of judging it.

name: Logan Cooper
q1: Stretch, smoothie, then maybe painting while a podcast rambles in the background. Low effort, high satisfaction.
q2: I’ll bring it up gently the first time. If it happens again, I get firm — fairness matters to me.
q3: Mixing paint colors until I accidentally make something beautiful.
q4: I can quote entire stand-up specials from memory.
q5: When someone calls out my creativity without making it sound like a hobby.

name: Grayson Ellis
q1: Blanket burrito, tea, and watching rain hit the window. Absolute introvert heaven.
q2: I prefer writing out my feelings; I speak clearer on paper than out loud.
q3: That first sip of cold water after brushing my teeth — weirdly satisfying.
q4: I overanalyze text punctuation; a period feels like an attitude.
q5: When someone tells me they like my calm energy instead of mistaking it for boredom.

name: Xavier Porter
q1: Sundays are for catching up on sleep and half-finished projects. I’ll start something creative, get distracted making brunch, then finish it at midnight.
q2: I listen first, then clarify what I heard. Most problems shrink once people feel understood.
q3: The sound of scissors perfectly cutting wrapping paper.
q4: I look spontaneous, but I plan every trip down to snacks.
q5: When someone notices the care behind my “easygoing” vibe.

name: Diana Reed
q1: Pancakes, slow music, maybe folding laundry if I feel ambitious. I like a day that feels like breathing out.
q2: I need calm tone and real words. Sarcasm shuts me down instantly.
q3: When a grocery line suddenly moves faster than expected.
q4: I cry at happy endings, not sad ones.
q5: When someone remembers how I take my coffee without asking.

name: Tina Banks
q1: Long run, cold shower, then I turn my phone off. The world can wait until Monday.
q2: Say it straight. I can handle honesty; I can’t handle guessing.
q3: Perfectly timed green lights on an empty street.
q4: I journal almost every night — even if it’s one sentence.
q5: When someone respects my need for momentum, not just peace.

name: Eden Martinez
q1: I make breakfast for everyone in the house, even the hung-over roommate. Feeding people is how I say “I love you.”
q2: I take things personally, but I always circle back with an apology if I went too far.
q3: Wiping a foggy mirror clean in one smooth swipe.
q4: I still talk to plants like they understand me.
q5: When someone appreciates softness as strength, not weakness.

name: Manaj Patel
q1: Stretch, sunlight, and a playlist that makes the morning feel cinematic. I let the day decide what happens next.
q2: I try to keep emotion and ego separate — not easy, but I’m working on it.
q3: Finding a new street artist’s work on a random wall.
q4: I’m more romantic than I let on; I just hide it behind humor.
q5: When someone calls me out kindly instead of letting me spiral.

name: Aarav Ellis
q1: I brew tea, put on a record, and spend an hour rearranging furniture for no reason.
q2: I don’t raise my voice; I raise questions. That usually gets us somewhere.
q3: Matching fonts on a project — instant dopamine.
q4: I’m a minimalist who hoards digital photos.
q5: When someone notices I’m overstimulated and dims the light without me asking.

name: Meera Smith
q1: Breakfast burrito, sunglasses, and a drive up the hills just to watch the city wake up.
q2: I like solutions, not circles. Let’s fix it, forgive it, and move on.
q3: A perfectly folded burrito that doesn’t leak — rare art.
q4: I’m sentimental about old cars and bad playlists.
q5: When someone laughs at the dumb stories I tell from high school.

name: Ishaan Jordan
q1: I stay in bed until sunlight hits my face, then make coffee I don’t even need.
q2: I get quiet first. Not cold — just thinking. Then I’ll say exactly what I mean.
q3: Fresh socks right out of the dryer.
q4: I love learning random facts; I fall down Wikipedia holes for fun.
q5: When someone gets that silence isn’t disinterest, it’s processing.

name: Lucia Reyes
q1: Cleaning playlist on, windows open, and the satisfaction of floors that actually shine.
q2: I want to solve it fast — tension lingers in my head for days otherwise.
q3: Watching soap bubbles gather before rinsing them away.
q4: I’m way funnier when I’m nervous.
q5: When someone tells me I make their space calmer.

name: Aria Watson
q1: Biking to nowhere particular, ending up wherever smells like coffee and baked goods.
q2: I talk things through once emotions cool off — logic first, heart second.
q3: Finding heart-shaped rocks on trails.
q4: I still send postcards when I travel.
q5: When someone shares silence comfortably, no filler needed.

name: Hiro Park
q1: Wake up late, coffee in one hand, crossword in the other. The rest of the day just unfolds — maybe a walk, maybe laundry, maybe nothing at all.
q2: I try to stay curious instead of defensive. “Tell me more” works better than “You’re wrong.”
q3: The sound of ice cracking when I pour a drink.
q4: I love corny motivational quotes more than I admit.
q5: When someone catches the quiet effort behind things I make look easy.

name: Liliana Park
q1: I make a breakfast sandwich, eat it in bed, and pretend the world doesn’t need me for a few hours.
q2: I think with my hands — if I’m pacing or cleaning, I’m processing. Let me move, then I’ll talk.
q3: Perfect avocado ripeness. I’ll brag about it.
q4: I save every concert wristband I’ve ever gotten.
q5: When someone calls me reliable but still fun.

name: Maria Reyes
q1: Tea, sunlight, and maybe painting my nails while a podcast rambles in the background.
q2: I listen until I understand, not just until it’s my turn.
q3: Peeling an orange in one perfect spiral.
q4: I have an unexpectedly dark sense of humor.
q5: When someone mirrors my energy — calm, kind, curious.

name: Rafael Vega
q1: I’ll throw together pancakes for friends who stayed over and then spend an hour talking about everything and nothing.
q2: I joke first, talk second. Humor helps me find the truth safely.
q3: When a stranger’s dog decides I’m worth saying hi to.
q4: I cry at sports movies every time.
q5: When someone teases me kindly — that’s my love language.

name: Jin Tran
q1: I run errands early so the rest of the day feels earned. Then it’s nap, snacks, and comfort shows.

q3: Folding warm towels straight out of the dryer.
q4: I can’t resist claw machines — I’ve actually won a few.
q5: When someone values stability instead of confusing it with boring.

name: Hector Banks

q3: The smell of sunscreen even when I’m not going anywhere.
q4: I can whistle almost any song after one listen.
q5: When someone respects quiet as connection, not distance.

name: Nova Ramirez
q1: I stay in bed reading news headlines and pretending I’m catching up on the world when I’m really just avoiding chores.

q3: Clicking a pen over and over when I’m thinking.
q4: I love karaoke but pretend I don’t.
q5: When someone laughs at my sarcasm instead of flinching.

name: Quinn Lopez

q2: I talk softly but I’m honest — no drama, just truth.
q3: Finding a feather on the ground and pretending it’s a sign.
q4: I have a secret dream of opening a tiny café one day.
q5: When someone notices small shifts in my mood before I say anything.

name: Amari Garcia
q1: I blast music and deep clean like I’m auditioning for a cleaning commercial. Then I order takeout because cooking feels illegal that day.

q3: Getting a text that says “made me think of you.”
q4: I still make birthday cards by hand.
q5: When someone appreciates effort more than perfection.

name: Devon Hernandez
q1: Biking to the park, sketchbook in my bag, staying until the sun hits that perfect sleepy angle.

q5: When someone listens all the way to the end of my story before reacting.

q1: Coffee first, always. Then I wander through the house fixing one random thing and ignoring three others. Progress, sort of.

q5: When someone asks follow-up questions instead of assuming they know what I mean.

name: Sarah Carter

q3: When a song ends exactly as I park the car.

q5: When someone makes space for me to finish a thought instead of rushing in.

name: María Wong
